questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Prestige, academic opportunity and location

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience, can highly recommend Dartmouth college :D

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a guided tour around campus by the Exchange program coordinator at Dartmouth. She mostly showed us around campus, but I feel like she left some crucial details out about some of the more cultural things at Dartmouth.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have explained some of the social aspects a little better, especially the dinning options and things like that a little better - as well as showing us the gym and things like that.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You were assigned housing, prior to that you had to fill a survey out with priorities about if you wanted 0,1 or 2 roommates. I asked for either 0 or 1 and ended up having two roomates the first term and zero the second term so it felt a little pointless filling it out.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a mandatory meal plan at college - which was quite extensive but a little expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its a bit of a lottery some of the exchange students had quite nice housing and some of the other ones had less nice housing. Id defintely try my hardest to avoid the choates or the lodge.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally quite easy and we were allowed to take any of the courses available to undergrad students at Dartmouth except for a couple courses where they did not have space due to graduating seniors needing the class for their majors .

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you go onto Darthub, onto course registration and then select the courses you want. If the courses have any pre reqs then you have to either message the professor or one of the course administrators which will usually give you an override. you can find the courses available that term on the department websites or by just googling Dartmouth courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Honestly not sure, did not need any help, but there is a career/course help on campus who you could probably ask.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 95% - there was one course in winter term that i really wanted but was unable to take due to lack of space.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for courses the day that course selection opens up, as some of the courses are a little competitive to get into especially the computer science ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally the level quite high, but I also took ambitious courses when I was there such as the advanced micro economics class. Generally the level in the Economics and Government courses are quite high while the ENVS department left something to be desired.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite differently some of the classes were taught as Socratic style seminars such as theory of finance and misinformation and conspiracy theory. And then some of the other classes were more lecture based such as the ENVS and game theory class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON35:Game Theory 
ECON36: Theory of Finance
ENVS56 : Environmental economics and governance

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON38: THE ECONOMICS OF GOVERNMENTS AND PUBLIC POLICY
GOVT30.4 : Political Misinformation and Conspiracy Theories 
ECON81: Topics of Advanced Microeconomics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Game theory - Incredible professor 
Misinformation and Conspiracy theories - Wonderful professor, interesting topics and you get to write a paper about something you are passionate about. 
Advanced microeconomics - Same professor as Game theory, a little difficult course but you learn a lot :D

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not sure i really encountered any unexpected costs other than toothpaste and deodorant being relatively expensive compared to back home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Personal hygiene products like shower gel, shampoo and deodorant

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is strong greek life at college that is super inclusive, if you come in fall term then you can also rush the frats or sororities as an exchange student.

There are a bunch of clubs and activities such as the badminton club or the DOC

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The greek life is a good one if you want the traditional college experience. Otherwise the dancing clubs or sports clubs are a good way of making friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out enjoy the night life, go on a hike or study - you will need to spend some of your weekends studying :D

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy - people are quite friendly, but it might take a little bit of time to get close to people as it is easy to make new friends but a little more difficult to make close friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the frats - that is the best place for meeting new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The small talk can sometimes be a little socially draining if you are not used to constantly interacting with people. Also having dinner with people everyday can be a little draining, but you get used to it and appreciate it. If you have roomies it might be a little difficult to have some personal time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness and how willing random people were to talk to you and invite you to random things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1)Be aware that the course load can be quite heavy - so there might be weeks with a lot of work, but also great social opportunities such as green key, which is the equivalent of Ku festival but a lot better. 
2) Be smart about the courses you select, that they are not all reading heavy, test heavy or participation heavy. Its a good idea to be a little strategic about the courses you select. 
3) Be open minded and put yourself out there - you will not make friends if you do not put yourself out there for people to talk t0 you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it - It flys by super fast.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The best part was getting to make a bunch of new friends from all over the world who were all incredibly kind.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Either getting used to the cold and darkness in winter term or Econ81

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
